name: X-not-Y contrastive framing (AI writing tell)
description: Cliche contrastive framing in either order — "not X, it is Y" or "X, not Y" — a well-known LLM prose tic. Background scan confirmed instances in 10/10 essays (31 total occurrences) — this is a near-universal tic across the whole corpus, not isolated to one essay.

name: Run-on / overlong sentences
description: Sentences overloaded with multiple independent clauses (often stitched with em-dashes or colons) that should be split — readers lose the thread or the sentence just runs too long. Background scan found 39 total occurrences across all 10 essays — near-universal.

name: Punctuation-as-crutch overuse (em-dashes, colons)
description: Em-dashes and colons used at a much higher frequency than natural prose (4-9 em-dashes and 2-5 colons per ~300-word essay) — classic AI-writing stylistic tell. Confirmed by direct computation across all 10 essays: 4-9 em-dashes and 2-5 colons each — consistently elevated, no exceptions.

name: Word count exceeds requested limit
description: Prompt asks for a "300 word essay" but the model both claims and delivers more (e.g. ≈310 claimed here; actual body is 339 words) — instruction-following miss on an explicit constraint. Confirmed by direct computation: ALL 10/10 essays exceed the requested 300 words (by 3 to 71 words).

name: Punctuation inconsistency in rhetorical question chains
description: A question mark ends a clause mid-sentence (e.g. "...how good is it? but where does it run...") without capitalizing the next word, leaving it ambiguous whether it is one sentence or two. Background scan confirmed this is an isolated instance — only 1 occurrence in the whole 10-essay corpus (trace_02).
example_quotes: the decisive question about an AI system is no longer how good is it? but where does it run, and who can switch it off?

name: Redundant / circular phrasing
description: Restates the same idea with overlapping words rather than adding information, e.g. "remain within national jurisdiction where policy or law requires it" (jurisdiction and policy/law overlap). Background scan found additional instances in trace_06 and trace_07 (recurring: the 'Digital Public Good(s)' certification phrase repeats near-identically across multiple essays).

grounded, real-world scenarios

name: Staccato-then-sprawl sentence rhythm
description: A very short punchy sentence is immediately followed by a long, list-heavy sentence — a repeating rhythmic pattern rather than natural variation. Background scan found 9 additional instances across 9/10 essays (trace_05 excluded) — this rhythmic pattern is near-universal across the corpus.
example_quotes: The result reframes who gets to build. Professors, programme managers, tech leads and students all become authors rather than petitioners...
The strategic ambition is larger. By pushing open source and abstraction, we intend workflows to become a new layer that commoditises the models beneath them...

What distinguishes this approach is the unit of analysis. We evaluate the AI workflow — a human-readable chain of prompts, abstracted model calls, retrieval documents and tool calls, paired with use-case-specific "golden" input and output datasets — rather than an abstract model score.

The foundation is abstraction. We reduce AI systems to workflows — human-readable chains of prompts, abstracted model calls, retrieval documents and tool calls — so that the model itself becomes a swappable component.

Deployment matters just as much as authoring. A workflow can ship instantly to the channels the Global South actually uses — WhatsApp, Telegram, Facebook, SMS, voice and web — so usability testing happens with real users, in real languages, in days rather than months.

Gooey.AI inverts that relationship. We abstract everything into AI workflow recipes: small, collaborative artefacts combining LLM prompts, chained model calls, tool calls and code snippets, RAG documents, analytics, and use-case-specific golden evaluation datasets.

The method is deliberately hands-on. Through public prompt-a-thons and workshops held in Bangalore, Delhi and beyond, participants probe model behaviour, document what they find, and contribute toward more inclusive datasets and tools.
Openness at Gooey operates at three levels. The first is the codebase — inspectable, deployable and forkable, which means an organisation that adopts us cannot be locked out of what it has built.
The composition matters. A team of only engineers would have built a developer tool; a team of only impact practitioners would have built a report.

Rigour matters as much as reach. Our agricultural advisory evaluation work is published at gooey.ai/ageval, built on golden evaluation datasets developed with partner organisations who supply grounded, real-world scenarios.
Mental health is an unforgiving test case. Advice must be safe, culturally legible and delivered in the user's own language, often through a phone rather than a clinic.

name: Excessive enumeration / list overload

name: Conjunction-initial sentence opening (And/But)
